'''Lamine Diane''' (born November 7, 1997) is a Senegalese professional [[basketball]] player who plays for the [[Cape Town Tigers]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball|Cal State Northridge Matadors]]. He was named the [[Big West Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big West Player of the Year]] in both 2019 and 2020.

==High school and college career==
Diane, the son of Senegal national team player [[Keletigui Diane]], first began playing basketball at the age of nine, though he was initially more interested in soccer.<ref name="soto">{{cite news |last1=Soto |first1=Andres |title=Far from home: Inside Lamine Diane's pursuit of his NBA dream |url=https://sundial.csun.edu/163043/sports/far-from-home-inside-lamine-dianes-pursuit-of-his-nba-dream/ |access-date=November 8, 2021 |work=The Daily Sundial |date=February 12, 2021}}</ref> He came to the United States in 2015 to play high school basketball at [[Findlay Prep]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]]. He came into his own in his second season as he tripled his scoring average from 5 to 16 points per game.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Jordan|first1=Jason|title=Findlay Prep's Senegalese forward Lamine Diane starring in just his second year in the U.S.|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/findlay-preps-senegalese-forward-lamine-diane|accessdate=April 1, 2019|work=[[USA Today]]|date=January 17, 2017}}</ref> He committed to [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball|Cal State Northridge]], redshirting the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]] to concentrate on academics and to allow a wrist injury to heal.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Whicker|first1=Mark|title=The numbers are there for CSUN's Lamine Diane, but there's more to come|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/01/07/whicker-the-numbers-are-there-for-csuns-lamine-diane-but-theres-more-to-come/|accessdate=April 1, 2019|work=[[Los Angeles Daily News]]|date=January 7, 2019}}</ref> As a redshirt freshman, Diane averaged 24.8 points, 11.2 rebounds and 2.2 blocked shots per game and led the nation in field goals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2019-04-25/5-players-who-could-lead-mens-college-basketball-scoring |title=5 players who could lead men's college basketball in scoring in 2020 |last=Northam |first=Mitchell |date=April 25, 2019 |website=NCAA.com |access-date=May 20, 2019 }}</ref>  At the close of the season became the first player in history to win the [[Big West Conference]]'s Player, Freshman and Newcomer of the Year awards in the same year.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Pilla|first1=Sarah|title=CSUN Has Potential NBA Draft Pick on its Roster|url=https://spectrumnews1.com/ca/san-fernando-valley-ventura/sports/2019/03/14/lamine-diane-named-player-of-the-year-in-the-big-west-conference|accessdate=April 1, 2019|work=spectrumnews1.com|date=March 14, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Miller|first1=Kerry|title=Lamine Diane Is CBB's Unknown Freshman Putting Up No. 1 Pick Deandre Ayton Stats|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2819294-lamine-diane-is-cbbs-unknown-freshman-putting-up-no-1-pick-deandre-ayton-stats|accessdate=April 1, 2019|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=February 7, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Big West Announces 2018-19 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team|url=http://www.bigwest.org//story.asp?story_id=21020|accessdate=April 1, 2019|work=[[Big West Conference]]|date=March 11, 2019}}</ref>

For his sophomore season, Diane was named to the preseason All-Big West team.<ref>{{cite news|title=UC Irvine Picked To Repeat In Tight Men's Basketball Media Vote|url= https://bigwest.org/news/2019/10/24/uc-irvine-picked-to-repeat-in-tight-mens-basketball-media-vote.aspx|accessdate=November 30, 2019|work=[[Big West Conference]]|date=October 24, 2019}}</ref> However, he was ruled academically ineligible for the first semester by the NCAA.<ref>{{cite news|title= 4 takeaways from Pepperdine's 94-82 win over CSUN|url= https://www.midmajormadness.com/2019/11/13/20963455/takeaways-from-pepperdines-94-82-win-over-csun-recap-lamine-diane-mark-gottfried-kessler-edwards|accessdate=November 30, 2019|work=[[SBNation]]|date=November 13, 2019}}</ref> At the close of the regular season, Diane was awarded his second straight conference Player of the Year honor.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://bigwest.org/news/2020/3/9/big-west-reveals-2019-20-mens-basketball-all-conference-team.aspx|title=Big West Reveals 2019-20 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team|publisher=[[Big West Conference]] |date=March 9, 2020 |accessdate=March 9, 2020}}</ref> He averaged 25.6 points, 10.2 rebounds, two blocks and 1.7 steals per game. Following the season Diane declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Soto |first1=Andres |title=Lamine Diane declares for NBA Draft |url=https://sundial.csun.edu/157147/sports/lamine-diane-declares-for-nba-draft/ |accessdate=April 8, 2020 |work=The Daily Sundial |date=April 7, 2020}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Delaware Blue Coats (2021–2022)===
On December 3, 2020, Diane signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Team Signs Lamine Diane |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-signs-lamine-diane |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 3, 2020 |date=December 3, 2020}}</ref> On December 7, he was waived by the 76ers.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=sixers |number=1336071738967220225 |date=December 7, 2020 |title=We have waived Lamine Diane and Justin Robinson.}}</ref> He was then added to the roster of the 76ers' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Delaware Blue Coats]], making his debut on February 11, 2021, and scoring three points, blocking two shots and pulling down two rebounds.<ref name="soto" /> On October 25, he re-signed with Delaware.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Delaware Blue Coats|number=1452778827533492232|title=Let's go Camping. #TrainingCamp | #GetYourCoatsOn|user=blue_coats|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=December 19, 2021}}</ref> On February 3, 2022, Diane was ruled out for the season with a shoulder injury.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lamine Diane: Done for season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/lamine-diane-done-for-season/ |access-date=February 13, 2022 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 3, 2022}}</ref>

=== Cape Town Tigers (2023-present) ===
In October 2023, the [[Cape Town Tigers]] from South Africa announced they had signed Diane on their social media.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CyFfpnYu3C4/ |access-date=2023-10-24 |website=www.instagram.com}}</ref> He was, however, not on the roster of the Tigers for the [[2024 BAL qualification|2024 BAL qualification tournament]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cape Town Tigers at the Africa Champions Clubs ROAD TO B.A.L. 2024 2023 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/africaleague/2024/qualifiers/team/Cape-Town-Tigers |access-date=2023-11-28 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}</ref>
